newsitem.title: CHINA: Russian foreign minister starts China visit.
newsitem.headline: Russian foreign minister starts China visit.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived in Shanghai on Sunday at the start of a three-day visit to China, Russian consular officials said.
He arrived at Shanghai's Hongqiao airport from Tokyo after securing a major improvement in relations with Japan.
Primakov was due to spend a day in the city before going to Beijing on Monday morning to meet Chinese leaders.
He was scheduled to meet his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen on Monday and President Jiang Zemin at the Great Hall of the People on Tuesday afternoon.
On Sunday, he was expected to meet a vice-mayor of Shanghai, attend a reception in his honour and visit the Jinqiao Export Processing Zone in the Pudong New Area, the officials said.

The city wants to make Pudong, on the east side of the Huangpu river, its commercial and business centre, and the area, a mass of skyscrapers and construction sites, is a stop for most visiting dignitaries.
The city's stock exchange plans to move to Pudong next year, with the rest of the city's exchanges to follow. Pudong has also attracted a large number of major manufacturing joint ventures.
On Sunday evening, Primakov was due to meet officials of Russia's consulate in Shanghai, the officials said. It is Primakov's first visit to the country's industrial and commercial capital.

Japan released $500 million in long-delayed aid to Russia on Friday and Moscow offered the joint development of a group of disputed islands in the biggest steps forward in their ties since the end of the Cold War.
In a meeting with Primakov, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said Japan was ready to resume disbursing a 1991 aid package consisting of $500 million in Export-Import Bank loans.

The aid package, originally only for "humanitarian assistance" and restricted to medical projects, was frozen in 1991 because of political and economic turmoil in Russia following the collapse of the Soviet Union.
